sourceInformation.perspective: Side-on horizontal scrolling; two-dimensional x/y flight plane
sourceInformation.tech: JavaScript, Canvas 2D, Web Audio; full my-3D2dge v0.89.1 at 8ecc2f62353761187bdfe226f327b7ea5d2eb691; unmodified AI Hub session client v1.4.0 / protocol v1 at 35a1047f2067b2af3de3943f0fe452f39105d869
sourceInformation.artDirection: Original shaded pixel spacecraft, violet prison crystals, animated radial enemies, layered orbital scenery; native palette ramps, sprites and material/part shapes
sourceInformation.animation: Native E.anim sprite clips, continuous banking/cannon/thruster poses, mine deployment states, fracture, boarding trails, field collapse and carrier breakup
sourceInformation.audio: Original layered pulse/arpeggio music, synthesized effects and formant radio gibberish; no audio files; initial music gain 0.10
sourceInformation.online: Standalone solo and 1–2 couch shared-ship co-op; authoritative 1–2 AI Hub shared-world operation, authenticated role intentions, reliable full snapshots, disconnect handoff, tied team results and read-only online diagnostics. AI Hub supplies remote transport and lifecycle.
sourceInformation.testing: Unlimited functional headless/browser checks and ordinary-action full playthroughs were allowed. Used native Node drawing/simulation, standard-pad stubs, phone/tablet touch profiles, Chromium/Firefox/WebKit, actual two-copy Hub rounds, offline audio levels and 1920×1080/mobile screenshot review. Physical controllers, real touch hardware, iOS Safari, TV viewing and human listening were unavailable; human first-run duration is unknown. No FPS acceptance gates.
sourceInformation.research: Read the original rules and visually inspected two Odyssey2.info screenshots. Verified the supplied recording as the Odyssey² cartridge review and inspected 66 storyboard samples at five-second intervals; continuous playback and original sound were inaccessible, so exact original sound is unknown.
sourceInformation.environment: Codex CLI (headless); Linux / Ubuntu 26.04.1 on WSL2; Node 24.21.0; Python Playwright 1.63

testingFeedback: 25 unique defects were caught by automated checks and visual/integration review; all repaired. Repeated failures and test-harness mistakes are excluded.
2 critical issues: an incorrect renderer buffer reference prevented drawing, and closing the root menu could strand the front end.
The ordinary-action operation and two-copy shared-ship playthroughs proved rescue, mine ownership, every carrier phase, extraction and matching final network ledgers without cheats.
The first multi-touch test released the wrong CDP contact. Its early burst failures described the test harness; correcting the payload made the check useful.
engineFeedback: The dependency-free pixel renderer, palette ramps, sprite clips and controller-aware HTML shell made a coherent foundation.
Yes. I initially used r.g instead of r.ctx, and the native device-claim and menu-owner behavior needed explicit shared-ship adapters.
The deterministic rescue director, swept collision and unique rescue/score ledgers, with one authoritative ship shared across local and remote seats.
Tracing input, pause, device-claim and scene lifetimes so reconnects and local overlays preserved the same mission rules.
No core engine edits. Added original native sprites, clips, materials and shapes; a TV Shell theme; focused-seat menu routing; and semantic input/network adapters.
Document the renderer buffer and provide public hooks for menu ownership and controller reassignment, with a shared-ship example.
promptFeedback: The rescue-first operation, explicit round lifecycle and exact delivery schema gave the work a clear finish.
The SOURCE filename token needed filesystem normalization; I used Freedom-Fighters-1982. The requested human first-run pacing remains unmeasured.
Making controller ownership, disconnects, local overlays, checkpoint resets and authoritative network state agree across every input mode.
Include locally pinned engine and Hub files plus a compact acceptance checklist; retain the scenario tests and metadata schema.

aiHub.name: Freedom Moonriders
aiHub.description: Thread a living minefield, free crystal captives and dismantle a prison carrier. Fly solo or share one ship: a pilot steers while a navigator aims and commits hyperspace.
aiHub.controls: WASD / left stick fly; mouse / right stick aim; click / Space / R2 / Cross fire; Shift / L2 hyperspace; Escape / Options console; touch: left drag, right tap.
